extracted.intended_audience: authors/playwrights/contributors to periodical essays and general educated readers interested in satire, theatre, and moral writing
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive advice for composing and publishing Spectator-style essays and stage comedies that instruct or amuse without corrupting morals; includes editorial submission policy and guidance on suitable theatrical subjects and audience conduct. Emphasis on morality, honesty, and avoiding spectacle or lewdness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish contributors' papers entire and without alteration
rubrics_metrics.description: I am resolved for the Future to publish any 'Spectator' that deserves it, entire, and without any Alteration; assuring the World (if there can be Need of it) that it is none of mine and if the Authors think fit to subscribe their Names, I will add them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial policy: previously the editor adapted submissions to his style, but will now print deserving papers in their native dress and colours without dressing or excising them. Practical note: authors may have the option of subscribing their names; the editor will append them if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver value to the reader (two‑pence worth of mirth or instruction)
rubrics_metrics.description: I would not advise any one to take it in, who after the Perusal of it, does not find himself Two-pence the wiser, or the better Man for it; or who upon Examination, does not believe that he has had Two-pennyworth of Mirth or Instruction for his Money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each issue/page should give readers either genuine instruction or proper mirth commensurate with its cost; editorial/self-check: ensure content repays the reader's expense with either moral improvement or entertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not propagate false notions or launder base methods in practical counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Good Lectures to young Traders may have very good Effects on their Conduct: but beware you propagate no false Notions of Trade; let none of your Correspondents impose on the World, by putting forth base Methods in a good Light, and glazing them over with improper Terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When offering practical advice (e.g., on trade), avoid praising unethical shortcuts; do not call noise industry nor impudence courage, nor misattribute bankruptcy or success to misleading causes. Use exemplars (Honestus vs Fortunatus) to contrast honest modest profit with imposition-based fortunes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be skeptical of irrelevant credentials and spectacle
rubrics_metrics.description: There is something unaccountably taking among the Vulgar in those who come from a great Way off... The Doctor is lately come from his Travels, and has practised both by Sea and Land, and therefore Cures the Green Sickness, long Sea Voyages, Campains, and Lying-Inn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate claims on relevant evidence, not impressive but irrelevant details (foreign travel, long practice, family anecdotes). Anti-patterns: accepting distant origin, exotic trappings, or unrelated personal anecdotes as proof of competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on amazement or novelty in place of substance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Art of managing Mankind, is only to make them stare a little, to keep up their Astonishment, to let nothing be familiar to them, but ever to have something in your Sleeve, in which they must think you are deeper than they are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning against techniques that produce wonder without real merit (twine-cord weather predictors, dried sea-monsters, Latin phrases to impress). For serious writers, prefer substance and relevant argument over theatrical gimmicks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish between mirth and lewdness
rubrics_metrics.description: When Persons of a low Genius attempt this kind of Writing, they know no difference between being Merry and being Lewd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy should aim for genuine wit and amusement, not erotic or coarse shock-value. Avoid content that confuses laughter with indecency; scrutinize whether a joke degrades taste rather than delights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatre should promote morality and refine the audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Were our English Stage but half so virtuous as that of the Greeks or Romans, we should quickly see the Influence of it in the Behaviour of all the Politer Part of Mankind. ... Were our Plays subject to proper Inspections and Limitations, we might not only pass away several of our vacant Hours in the highest Entertainments; but should always rise from them wiser and better than we sat down to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plays ought to contribute to the advancement of morality and the reformation of the age; consider tempering subject matter and presentation to make theatre suitable for polite society and beneficial to public morals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent vices so they do not appear laudable
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever Vices are represented upon the Stage, they ought to be so marked and branded by the Poet, as not to appear either laudable or amiable in the Person who is tainted with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When depicting vice, ensure the dramatic framing or authorial comment makes clear its disapproval. Avoid portraying immoral characters in ways that invite admiration or imitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never choose improper subjects for ridicule (avoid subjects that evoke horror or pity)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Subject is improper for Ridicule, if it is apt to stir up Horrour and Commiseration rather than Laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select comic targets that naturally invite laughter; avoid topics (e.g., serious violations of the marriage bed, traumatic events) that more readily provoke pity or horror. Example: Terence does not base comedy on breaches of the marriage-bed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hooting, malicious raillery, and gratuitous cruelty in humour
rubrics_metrics.description: There is neither Mirth nor Good Humour in hooting a young Fellow out of Countenance; nor that it will ever constitute a Wit, to conclude a tart Piece of Buffoonry with a 'what makes you blush?' ... To speak what they know is shocking, proceeds from ill Nature, and a Sterility of Brain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience behaviour and comic practice should eschew cruel heckling or mean-spirited 'jokes' that shame others. Repeated over-bearing insolence is a sign of dulness; good humour should not aim merely to disoblige.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim ridicule at what is criminal or immoral, not merely unfashionable
rubrics_metrics.description: I have endeavoured to make nothing Ridiculous that is not in some measure Criminal. I have set up the Immoral Man as the Object of Derision: In short, if I have not formed a new Weapon against Vice and Irreligion, I have at least shewn how that Weapon may be put to a right Use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use satire as a tool against vice and irreligion rather than to mock eccentricity or unfashionableness. Ensure targets of ridicule are deserving of moral censure so the satire has ethical purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors should provide themes/prompts and set deadlines for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: I think the best way of promoting this generous and useful Design, will be by giving out Subjects or Themes of all Kinds whatsoever... The Thesis propos'd for the present Exercise of the Adventurers to write Spectators, is MONEY, on which Subject all Persons are desired to send their Thoughts within Ten Days after the Date hereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical editorial guideline: issue concrete themes and time-limits to solicit focused contributions; include a preamble on public benefit to attract diverse hands. This controls quality and coherence of submissions.
